title: Differentiation Module 3 Lesson 2: Optimisation in Geometry and Vector Contexts custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A rectangle has a fixed perimeter of $20\text{ cm}$. Use differentiation to find the dimensions of the rectangle that maximize its area.
A closed cylinder has a fixed volume of $54\pi\text{ cm}^3$. Express the total surface area $A$ in terms of the base radius $r$, and find the value of $r$ that minimizes $A$.
Find the exact coordinates of the points on the parabola $y = x^2$ that are closest to the point $(0, 2)$ by minimizing the square of the distance.
A sector of a circle of radius $r\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta$ radians has a fixed perimeter of $16\text{ cm}$. Find the value of $r$ that maximizes the area of the sector.

An open rectangular box with a square base of side length $x\text{ cm}$ and vertical height $h\text{ cm}$ has a total exterior surface area of $48\text{ cm}^2$. Find the value of $x$ for which the volume of the box is a maximum, and state this maximum volume.

A piece of wire of length $12\text{ m}$ is bent to form the boundary of a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of lengths $x\text{ m}$ and $y\text{ m}$. Find the exact value of $x$ for which the area of the triangle is stationary.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is inscribed in the first quadrant under the line $y = 4 - \frac{2}{3}x$, with one vertex at the origin $(0, 0)$, one vertex at $(x, 0)$, one vertex at $(x, y)$, and one vertex at $(0, y)$, where $0 < x < 6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express the area $A$ of the rectangle in terms of $x$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the dimensions of the rectangle that maximize its area, and show that this maximum area is exactly half the area of the triangle formed by the line and the coordinate axes.

questions.prompt: A right circular cone of base radius $r\text{ cm}$ and height $h\text{ cm}$ is inscribed in a sphere of fixed radius $6\text{ cm}$, where $0 < h < 12$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that $r^2 = 12h - h^2$, and hence express the volume $V$ of the cone in terms of $h$ and $\pi$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use differentiation to find the value of $h$ for which $V$ is a maximum, and find this maximum volume in exact terms of $\pi$.

questions.prompt: A line $L$ in three-dimensional space passes through the point $A(1, 2, -1)$ with direction vector $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$. A variable point $P$ on $L$ has position vector $\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2t \\ 2 - t \\ -1 + 2t \end{pmatrix}$. Let $B$ be the fixed point $(4, -1, 3)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the square of the distance between $B$ and $P$ is given by $|\vec{BP}|^2 = 9t^2 - 34t + 34$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use calculus to find the value of $t$ that minimizes $|\vec{BP}|^2$, and verify that at this value, the vector $\vec{BP}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{d}$.

questions.prompt: A rain gutter is fabricated from a flat metal sheet of width $30\text{ cm}$ by bending up two edges of width $10\text{ cm}$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, creating a symmetrical trapezoidal cross-section with base $10\text{ cm}$ ($0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the cross-sectional area $A$ of the gutter is given by $A = 100\sin\theta(1 + \cos\theta)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the value of $\theta$ that maximizes $A$, and determine the exact maximum cross-sectional area in surd form.

questions.prompt: A solid right circular cone has base radius $6\text{ cm}$ and vertical height $12\text{ cm}$. A right circular cylinder of radius $r\text{ cm}$ and height $h\text{ cm}$ is inscribed in the cone ($0 < r < 6$).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show using similar triangles that $h = 12 - 2r$, and show that the total surface area $S$ of the cylinder (including both circular ends) is $S = 2\pi(12r - r^2)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the value of $r$ that maximizes $S$, and find the ratio of the maximum possible volume of the cylinder to the volume of the cone.

questions.prompt: A rigid thin beam is carried horizontally around a right-angled corner where a corridor of width $8\text{ m}$ meets a corridor of width $1\text{ m}$. The length $L(\theta)$ of a line segment touching the inside corner and both outer corridor walls is given by $L(\theta) = \frac{8}{\sin\theta} + \frac{1}{\cos\theta}$ for $0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that $\frac{\mathrm{d}L}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = 0$ when $\tan^3\theta = 8$, and deduce the exact value of $\tan\theta$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the maximum possible length of a rigid beam that can be navigated horizontally around this corner, giving your answer in exact simplest surd form.

questions.prompt: A lifeguard at point $A$ on a straight shoreline needs to reach a swimmer at point $B$, located $30\text{ m}$ perpendicular to the shore and $80\text{ m}$ downshore from $A$. The lifeguard runs along the beach at $5\text{ m/s}$ to a point $P$ at distance $x\text{ m}$ from $A$ ($0 \leq x \leq 80$), and then swims in a straight line from $P$ to $B$ at $3\text{ m/s}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the total time $T(x)$ taken in seconds to reach the swimmer is $T(x) = \frac{x}{5} + \frac{\sqrt{(80-x)^2 + 900}}{3}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that setting $\frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$ leads to the equation $16(80-x)^2 = 8100$, and find the value of $x$ that minimizes the total travel time.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum time $T_{\text{min}}$ in seconds, and show that running directly to the point opposite the swimmer ($x = 80$) takes longer.
